topic: What link budget trade-offs exist when balancing data rate and reliability in adverse weather for satellite backhaul links?
consensus_response: Satellite backhaul links face trade-offs between high data rates (e.g., W-band) and reliable performance in adverse weather.  This is driven by atmospheric attenuation, requiring careful antenna design (e.g., phased arrays), modulation techniques (e.g., adaptive coding & modulation - ACM), and beamforming to mitigate interference from rain, clouds, and gases.  Advanced modulation schemes like ACM are crucial for improving spectral efficiency in challenging environments. Adaptive beamforming dynamically adjusts signal direction based on atmospheric conditions, further enhancing reliability by reducing interference.
